# Observation agent: the whole site in one file
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/llms-full.txt

The site's pages in order, then the drafted documents, then the agent and skill definitions under .claude/ as used. The report is not included: it is https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.md.

# Observation agent
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/index.md

A system that runs inside Claude Code, reads all 3,240 messages of an email archive from Enron, finds the work that recurs, prices what could be automated at the brief's $85 an hour, and ties every claim to a message and a verbatim quote. One command, `/observe`, runs it; the outputs of one real run are committed beside the code, and this site is a reading copy of both.

## What the brief asked for, and where it is

One row per sentence of [the brief](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/brief.md) that can be checked, in the brief's order. Paths open the file on GitHub; pages are on this site.

## Start here

- [Open the dashboard](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/dashboard/index.html)
  The brief's dashboard runs on localhost with `node obs.mjs serve`; this is a copy of it with the same pages, data and messages, pre-written so nothing needs installing. Every number still opens down to its message.
- [Read the report](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.html)
  The same figures as a printable report, from the same data. Also [in Markdown](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.md).
- [Read the notes](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/notes.md)
  `NOTES.md`: how Claude Code was driven, where it went wrong, where the system is most likely wrong.
- [See the drafted documents](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md#documents)
  The working documents drafted for the opportunities above the threshold, with their evidence.
- [The run's facts and logs](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md)
  Timings by stage, subagents, quote checks and coverage, read from the run's own output.
- [The `.claude/` directory as used](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/claude-dir.md)
  The agents, skills, hooks and settings the run used, with their configuration read from the files.

[Screenshot: The dashboard's first screen: the automatable value a month with its counted and estimated parts, the three biggest findings, and the step chart of every process with the running total and the drafting line.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/overview.png)

## The submitted run in figures

- Automatable work a month (counted + estimated): $2,231 = $526 counted email time + $1,705 estimated hands-on work. 26.3 hours a month. The estimates put it between $1,243 and $4,989. Observed in 4 mailboxes, 1999-2002.
- Messages read (counted): 3,240; 3,201 after 39 duplicates.
- Recurring processes (counted): 60; 42 seen often enough to count in the total.
- Documents drafted (counted): 5; for the opportunities above the threshold.
- Run time (measured): 29.0 min; from the run log.
- Subagents started (counted): 130; 4 fix rounds.
- Quotes exact (counted): 2,684; 13 repaired, 0 rejected.

From run `20261019T134634Z` of 19 Oct 2026. Every figure above is read from the run's output when this site is built; [the run's facts](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md#facts) has the rest.

- [Report](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.html): The report of the submitted run, printable, with the same figures as the dashboard; report.md is the same report in Markdown.

# How to use what it produced
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/how-to-use.md

The run leaves four things to use: the dashboard, the report, the drafted documents, and the files in [`out/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out) they are built from. None of them needs a model call, and every figure in them leads back to messages in the archive.

## The dashboard

`node obs.mjs serve` (or `/serve` inside Claude Code) serves it on `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` by default, or on the next free port up to 8775, from the files the run built in `out/dashboard/`; the command prints the address it took; `/observe` starts it at the end of every run. It binds the local address only and fetches nothing from the network. The [copy on this site](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/dashboard/index.html) is the same pages and data, with every message written out as a file instead of served, so it needs nothing installed.

The views, in the header:

- **Overview**: the value stated simply, the three biggest findings with the quote behind each, the step chart of every process ranked by automatable dollars with the running total and the drafting line, the ranked table, and next steps.
- **All processes**: every process found, sortable, including the ones seen too rarely to count in the total.
- **Open loops**: threads whose last message in the archive is a chase, or a quote that is waiting for an answer, in the last 90 days of their mailbox.
- **How we measured**: the published rates, the tiers, the drafting threshold, the work estimates, the rounding, the identity folds, the flagged messages, the merge table, the quote checks and the run's facts.
- **Look up a message**: type or paste any message ID and read the message.

The theme button in the header switches between the system setting, light and dark.

[Screenshot: The dashboard's first screen: the automatable value a month with its counted and estimated parts, the three biggest findings, and the step chart of every process with the running total and the drafting line.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/overview.png)

### From a number to the message

Every figure is a button. A process's dollars open its formula, in two parts:

- the **counted** part: the email actions code counted on the trail (written, forwarded, chased, read), each at its published minutes and automatable share from [`config/effort-rates.json`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/config/effort-rates.json);
- the **estimated** part: the rounds code counted, times the minutes of hands-on work per round that the synthesizer estimated from quoted evidence, inside the bounds code sets.

Each count in the formula opens the list of messages it was counted from; each quote opens the message viewer, with the quoted span marked at the offsets the validator stored. Back and Escape step back through the drawer. On every figure the counted part is drawn solid and the estimated part hatched, with the estimate's own range as a band.

[Screenshot: A process page: how often it was seen and by whom, where it stalls with quotes, its open loops and its drafted document.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/process.png)

[Screenshot: A figure's formula: the counted email actions at published minutes beside the estimated work per round, each part opening its messages.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/formula.png)

[Screenshot: The message viewer: one email as the file holds it, the quoted span marked, with the buttons that copy the message ID and the git show command.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/viewer.png)

[Screenshot: The open loops view: threads whose last message is a chase or a wait for an answer, in the last 90 days of their mailbox.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/open-loops.png)

[Screenshot: How we measured: the published rates, the tiers, the drafting threshold and the counted and estimated parts of every figure.](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/assets/screenshots/methodology.png)

## Check a claim yourself

A message's ID is its path in the repository, trailing dot included: `corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1.` To check any quote against the raw file:

1. Open the message from a figure, a quote, or Look up a message.
2. Press **Copy message ID**, or **Copy the git show command** for the whole command.
3. In a clone of the repository, run `git show HEAD:"corpus/<mailbox>/<folder>/<n>."` The double quotes keep the shell away from the trailing dot. It prints the committed bytes; on macOS and Linux the same file is on disk.
4. Compare. The viewer shows the message exactly as the file holds it, headers, line ends and quoted-printable residue included, so the marked quote is a substring of what `git show` prints.

`node obs.mjs verify` repeats the check wholesale: it re-validates every committed extraction, synthesis and draft against its inputs and the corpus bytes, and fails on any difference. CI runs it on every push.

## The report

[`report.html`](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.html) is one file with its styles and two fonts inline, no script and no network, so it opens by double-click; page one prints alone on letter paper. [`report.md`](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.md) is the same report in Markdown. Both are rendered from one model of the report, built from the same data as the dashboard, so the numbers agree by construction ([`src/report/report.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/report.ts)).

## The drafted documents

The run drafts one working document for each opportunity above the threshold, of the type the synthesizer chose for the process: an SOP, a checklist, an email template or a template. Each is written for the team that does the work, to use the next morning. Code writes the title, the line under it and the people line; the drafter subagent writes the body under the headings of its type; code appends the Evidence section, message IDs with verbatim quotes checked against the raw bytes.

Two markers say what the mail does not settle. `[proposed: ...]` is a value the drafter proposed because the emails give none, such as a deadline; `[confirm still in force]` follows a rule that rests on a single email. Any other bracketed blank is for the owner to fill in. [The run's documents](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md#documents) are on this site, rendered and as Markdown.

## Re-scoring without a model

The rates and the estimates are files, so anyone can re-price the run in seconds:

- `node obs.mjs score --rates <file>` re-scores with other per-action minutes and automatable shares (start from a copy of [`config/effort-rates.json`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/config/effort-rates.json));
- `node obs.mjs score --estimates <file>` re-scores with other work estimates;
- `config/estimates.json`, when present, replaces the model's estimate for the processes it names and is labelled as an override everywhere.

A re-score with `--rates` or `--estimates` writes `out/opportunities.<name>.json` beside the run's own file and leaves the run's own figures alone. The rules are in [`src/run/score.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/run/score.ts); the arithmetic in [`src/metrics/score.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/metrics/score.ts).

## Where the code is

- [`src/report/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/src/report): the build stage. Every figure is pre-formatted with its kind and drill target ([`data.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/data.ts)), money only through one formatter ([`format.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/format.ts)), and every drill target is checked by a walk over the built files ([`targets.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/targets.ts)).
- [`src/serve/server.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/serve/server.ts): the local server, the message API and the detached start.
- [`dashboard/viewer.js`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/dashboard/viewer.js): the message viewer, which marks a quote at its stored offsets and never searches for it.

# How to run it
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/how-to-run.md

This is the repository's README, rendered.

# Observation agent

A system that reads a company's 3,240-message email archive inside Claude Code, finds its recurring work, and prices the automation opportunities at $85 an hour, with every claim cited to a message. It drafts working documents for the biggest opportunities and serves a dashboard on localhost.

[Project site](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/) · [NOTES.md](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/NOTES.md) (the two-page notes the brief asks for) · [BRIEF.md](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/BRIEF.md) (the assignment) · [llms.txt](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/llms.txt). The site is the one-stop reading copy; this repo is the thing itself.

## What this is

One command, `/observe`, runs the whole pipeline inside Claude Code. In order: prepare (read, parse, de-duplicate, thread and batch every message), taxonomy (one subagent proposes the recurring processes), extraction (many subagents in parallel tag every message with a process and a verbatim quote), merge, rollup (count rounds, people, email actions and stalls), synthesis (subagents describe each process and estimate its work), scoring, drafting (subagents write the documents), build (the dashboard data and the report) and serve. The model decides which messages belong to which process, and estimates the hands-on work per round from cited evidence, within bounds that code sets. Everything else is TypeScript: parsing, de-duplication, counting, the hours and dollars arithmetic, citation validation and the server.

## See the results without running anything

The outputs of the submitted run are committed in [`out/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out):

- [`out/report.html`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/out/report.html) and [`out/report.md`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/out/report.md): the report. `report.html` is self-contained and opens with a double-click.
- [`out/artifacts/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out/artifacts): the drafted documents.
- [`out/runs/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out/runs): the run logs.
- [`out/dashboard/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out/dashboard): the dashboard data.

`node obs.mjs serve` opens the dashboard on these files with no model call; `/serve` inside Claude Code does the same. The report has the same numbers as the dashboard. A copy of the report is on the site: [report.html](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/report.html). The site also carries a copy of the dashboard with every message pre-written, so you can click from any number to its message there with nothing installed: https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/dashboard/. The dashboard served below, on localhost, is the one the brief asks for.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22.18 or newer. It runs the TypeScript sources directly, so there is no build step. Claude Code's installer does not install Node; get it from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org).
- Git.
- Claude Code, signed in on a subscription whose plan includes Opus and Sonnet: the agent definitions pin Opus for the taxonomist, merger and synthesizer and Sonnet for the extractors and drafters (each file in [`.claude/agents/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/.claude/agents) names its model and effort). No API key and no API spend. The pipeline fetches nothing from the network; every model call goes through your Claude Code session.

`npm install` installs only the TypeScript compiler and Node's type definitions, for `npm run typecheck`. The pipeline, the server and the tests use nothing from `node_modules`.

## Get the code

### macOS and Linux

A plain `git clone` works. The corpus files' names end in a dot (`corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1.`) and check out as they are.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment.git obs
cd obs
npm install
```

### Windows

A plain `git clone` checks out nothing on Windows, not even the code, because Windows cannot create file names that end in a dot. Use this instead (PowerShell):

```powershell
git clone --no-checkout https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment.git obs
cd obs
git config core.protectNTFS false
git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/corpus/'
git checkout main
```

In Git Bash, prefix the sparse-checkout line with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`; otherwise Git Bash rewrites `/corpus/` into `C:/Program Files/Git/corpus/` and the exclusion silently fails:

```sh
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/corpus/'
```

The corpus then stays in Git's objects, off disk. The code reads every message from there (`git cat-file --batch`) and gets the same bytes macOS and Linux read from disk; a test checks that the two agree. Nothing is lost. Then run `npm install`, as on macOS and Linux.

## Run it

Start Claude Code in the folder:

```sh
claude
```

At the Claude Code prompt, type the one command:

```text
/observe
```

When the run is done, it prints the stages it ran, starts the dashboard in the background and prints its address (`Dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`), tries to open that address in your browser, and prints the run's status. The dashboard keeps running after you leave Claude Code; `node obs.mjs serve --stop` stops it. If a run stops part way (a crash, a closed window, a usage-limit pause), running `/observe` again resumes it from the run ledger.

### Warm and cold runs

The model outputs and the run ledger are committed, so the first run on a fresh clone is warm. It repeats no finished work and starts no subagent: it rebuilds the deterministic stages and ends with the dashboard.

To run cold, with every subagent again:

```text
/observe --force
```

`--force` clears the model outputs first. Every cold rehearsal since the drafting stage was added completed in under 30 minutes on our Windows machine, and so did the submitted run: 28 min 59 s, with 130 subagents started. A cold run asks the model again, so its process list, its merge and its work estimates can differ from the committed ones, and the dollar figures move with them. Counting and arithmetic are code and do not vary: the same model outputs give the same numbers on every rerun and every OS. If a cold run replaces the committed outputs, Git still holds the submitted run.

### Folder trust and permissions

The first time Claude Code opens a folder, it asks whether you trust it. Until the folder is trusted, Claude Code ignores the `permissions.allow` entry in the project's [`.claude/settings.json`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/settings.json). The run does not depend on it: the `/observe` skill's `allowed-tools` pre-approve its commands and its subagents while the skill runs, and the hooks apply either way. We checked this in a fresh, untrusted clone: the hooks all worked, and only that entry was ignored.

The hooks are in [`.claude/hooks/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/.claude/hooks), wired up in `settings.json`:

- The corpus guard (`guard-corpus.ts`, before every tool call) keeps each pipeline subagent to its own job's files and, during a run, refuses any tool call that names `corpus/` and any subagent that is not one of the five pipeline agents.
- The gate (`gate-subagent.ts`, when an extractor, synthesizer or drafter finishes) checks the output it wrote (schema, coverage, quotes against the raw messages, estimate rules, draft rules) and records the job as done, or as failed with a list of problems that goes back to a subagent as a fix round.
- The Stop hook (`gate-run.ts`) keeps the orchestrator going: when it would end its turn with a step ready to run, the hook hands it the next command.
- `log-event.ts` writes each subagent's start and stop to the run log in `out/runs/`.

### Unattended

The rehearsals ran headless, with stdin closed and the permission prompts off. From a macOS or Linux shell:

```sh
claude -p "/observe" --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none < /dev/null
```

For a cold run, pass `"/observe --force"` instead. On Windows, run it from Git Bash, the shell we tested there, with the prefix `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`; without it, Git Bash rewrites `/observe` into a path under Program Files and the skill never runs:

```sh
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 claude -p "/observe" --permission-mode auto --permission-prompts none < /dev/null
```

For a log of the orchestrator's turns, add `--output-format stream-json --verbose > ../observe-stream.jsonl`. Keep that file outside the repo: it carries the folder's absolute path. After a crash or a usage-limit pause, run the same command again; the run resumes from the ledger.

## Open the dashboard

```sh
node obs.mjs serve                        # foreground; Ctrl+C stops it
node obs.mjs serve --background --open    # returns at once, leaves it running, opens the browser
node obs.mjs serve --status               # prints the address of the running server
node obs.mjs serve --stop                 # stops the background server
```

`--port N` picks the port. `--background` reuses a server already running for this folder. The server binds 127.0.0.1 only. Inside Claude Code, `/serve` does the same as `--background --open`.

What you can do there:

- Click any number to see its formula and the messages behind it. Every figure shows which parts are counted and which are estimated.
- The message viewer shows the raw message with the cited quote marked, and a copy button with the ready `git show HEAD:"<id>"` command, so you can check the quote against the raw file yourself.
- The lookup box opens any message by its ID, which is its Git path with the trailing dot included (`corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1.`).

## Tests

```sh
npm test
npm run typecheck
```

No model is ever invoked: the tests stand in for the model stages with scripted fixtures. CI ([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) runs both on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows (Windows with the clone recipe above), then rebuilds the deterministic stages and re-checks every committed model output against the corpus. You can run those two steps yourself:

```sh
node obs.mjs prepare --force
node obs.mjs verify
```

We developed on Windows. macOS and Linux behaviour is proven by CI, not by a Mac at hand.

# The submitted run
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md

The outputs of one real run of `/observe` are committed in [`out/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out): run `20261019T134634Z` of 19 Oct 2026. Everything on this page is read from those files when the site is built.

## Run facts

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Run | `20261019T134634Z`, 19 Oct 2026 |
| Run time | 29.0 minutes: from each run’s first event to its last step of work, summed over the runs |
| Subagents started | 130: 1 taxonomist, 101 extractors, 1 merger, 21 synthesizers, 6 drafters |
| Fix rounds | 4 |
| Quotes checked against the raw bytes | 2,684 exact, 13 repaired, 0 rejected |
| Merge | 430 proposed keys; 81 mapped to a taxonomy key; 35 promoted processes; 266 aliases of promoted processes; 83 left unassigned; 0 demoted by the size check; 140 messages mapped; 475 messages in promoted processes; 115 messages left unassigned |
| Work estimates | 58 accepted, 2 missing, 0 overridden |
| Coverage | 3,240 files = 2,255 counted + 115 unassigned + 576 personal + 224 noise + 30 automated + 1 flagged + 39 duplicates |
| Headline (tiers A and B) | $2,231 a month = $526 counted + $1,705 estimated; the estimates put it between $1,243 and $4,989; 26.3 hours a month |
| Documents | 5 drafted, 0 exhausted, 0 skipped, 0 failed |
| Open loops | 169 threads end on a chase or a wait for an answer; 24 of them in the last 90 days of their mailbox |
| Identity folds | 57 addresses folded into another: 4 display name, 4 middle initial, 6 last name, 10 first last, 33 initial last |
| Contradictions dropped | 0 |
| Tagging accuracy (gold set) | 80.8% exact (42 of 52), 80.8% overlap, 73.1% role |

The same facts print with `node obs.mjs summary`, and the dashboard's How we measured shows them beside the figures they explain.

## What out/ holds

- The prepared corpus facts: the manifest of every message with its Git blob ID, the parsed messages, the duplicate groups, the threads and the people.
- Every model output and its check: the taxonomy, the extractions and their validated copies, the merge table, the syntheses, the drafting briefs and the drafts, each with a ledger file recording its cache key.
- What code made from them: the rollup, the scored opportunities, the drafted documents with their evidence, the dashboard data and the report.
- The run logs.

The dashboard runs on these files with no model call: `node obs.mjs serve`. Because the ledger is committed, the first `/observe` in a fresh clone finds every job current and starts no subagent; `/observe --force` runs cold. [Warm and cold runs](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/how-to-run.md#warm-and-cold-runs) has the detail.

## The dashboard copy on this site

The [dashboard here](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/dashboard/index.html) is the run's built dashboard copied as it is, with one change: its page is marked as the static copy, so the message viewer reads each message from a file beside the page instead of asking the local server. Every message of the manifest was written once through the same corpus reader the server uses, in the shape the server returns.

The copy holds 3,240 messages, 3,316 files in all, 15.5 MB. [Open it](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/dashboard/index.html).

# Architecture
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/architecture.md

One TypeScript pipeline with no runtime dependency, run from inside Claude Code by one skill. Code does everything that has to be exact; subagents do the judgement; code checks every model output before anything uses it. The full design, with every contract and decision, is [`.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## From the archive to the dashboard

Diagram: From the archive to the dashboard ([SVG](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/diagrams/pipeline.svg)). In words:

- The orchestrator above every stage: the `/observe` skill, which runs one command per turn, `node obs.mjs advance`. Each call runs every code step that is ready and names the subagents to start next.
- The corpus, kept in Git objects on Windows and on disk on macOS and Linux, is opened only by the corpus reader, which returns the same bytes from either.
- prepare (code): ingest, parse, de-duplicate, thread and batch every message.
- taxonomist (model, one call): proposes the list of recurring processes; code accepts it or sends back the problems.
- extractors (model, 99 batch jobs, 20 in flight): tag every message with process keys and verbatim quotes. The gate checks that every message is classified and every quote is in the raw bytes.
- merger (model, one call): places every process key the extractors proposed. The gate checks each key is placed once and sizes every promoted process on the messages behind it.
- rollup (code): counts rounds, people, email actions, reply gaps and stalls on the merged membership.
- synthesizers (model, groups of up to 4 processes, one wave): describe each process and estimate its hands-on minutes per round. The gate checks the estimate's bounds and citations.
- score (code): counted email time at the published rates, plus counted rounds times the checked estimate, at $85 an hour; then tiers, ranks and the drafting threshold.
- drafters (model, up to 8): one working document per opportunity above the threshold. The draft gate checks headings, quotes and figures.
- build (code): the dashboard data and the report, every figure pre-formatted with its drill target.
- serve (code): the dashboard on 127.0.0.1, each message read through the corpus reader.
- Key: code steps are plain boxes, model steps tinted boxes, gates amber pills.

### The stages

Every stage is a command of [`obs.mjs`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/obs.mjs); during a run `advance` calls them in order. Condensed from [section 4 of the design](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#4-pipeline-stages).

| Stage | Done by | Input | Output | Cache key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [prepare](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/pipeline/prepare.ts) | code | the corpus, through the [reader](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/corpus/reader.ts) | the manifest, parsed messages, duplicates, threads, people, batch files | skipped when the corpus listing, the code and every output are unchanged |
| [taxonomy](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/run/taxonomy.ts) | model, then the accept step | the taxonomy digest built by code | `out/taxonomy.json` | the digest and the taxonomist's definition |
| extract | model, then the [gate](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/validate-extraction.ts) | one batch file and the taxonomy | `out/extract/`, `out/validated/` | the batch, the taxonomy and the extractor's definition |
| [merge](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/run/merge.ts) | model, then the [accept step](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/merge.ts) | the merge input built by code | `out/merge.json` | the extractions, the taxonomy and the merger's definition |
| [rollup](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/metrics/rollup.ts) | code | validated extractions, the merge, threads, people | `out/rollup.json`, the synthesis inputs | reruns in seconds |
| synthesize | model, then the [gate](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/synthesis.ts) | one group input | `out/synthesis/validated/` | the group input and the synthesizer's definition |
| [score](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/metrics/score.ts) | code | rollup, syntheses, [`config/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/config) | `out/opportunities.json` | reruns |
| [artifacts prepare](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/run/artifacts.ts) | code | opportunities, rollup, syntheses | one brief per document | reruns |
| draft | model, then the [draft gate](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/artifacts.ts) | one brief | `out/artifacts/raw/`, `validated/` | the brief and the drafter's definition |
| artifacts collect | code | checked drafts and their briefs | `out/artifacts/<process>/<type>.md` | reruns |
| [build](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/build.ts) | code | everything above | `out/dashboard/`, the report, `out/run-summary.json` | the hashes of its inputs, recorded in `data.json` |
| [serve](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/serve/server.ts) | code | `out/dashboard/`, the corpus reader | the dashboard on 127.0.0.1 | nothing cached |

The ledger that records every job, its cache key and its state is [`src/run/ledger.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/run/ledger.ts): one file per job, so a rerun on an unchanged corpus repeats nothing and a crash or a usage-limit pause resumes where it stopped.

### The two places a model touches a number

1. **Membership.** Which messages belong to which process is judgement: the extractors tag each message, and the merger decides where each proposed key's messages count. Code then counts everything from that membership: rounds, people, email actions, windows. It checks first: every tag needs its own verbatim quote that passes validation, every proposed key is placed exactly once, and a promoted process must reach a minimum size on its own messages (`promote_min` in [`config/scoring.json`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/config/scoring.json)) or it is demoted and left unpriced.
2. **The work estimate.** For each process the synthesizer proposes the minutes of hands-on work one round takes (low, mid and high) and the share of that work that could be automated, citing the quotes it relied on. Code accepts it only inside fixed bounds (1 to 480 minutes, at most 80% automatable) and with evidence from at least three rounds and two senders, so one person's claim can never set a value. The mid value multiplies the counted rounds and nothing else; low and high give the range shown beside it; a file, `config/estimates.json`, can replace any estimate without a model call.

Everything else that produces a number is code: counts, windows, rates, tiers, ranks, the threshold, the arithmetic at $85 an hour and the rounding. See [`src/metrics/score.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/metrics/score.ts) and [Counted and estimated](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/design.md#counted-vs-estimated).

## Inside Claude Code

Diagram: Inside Claude Code ([SVG](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/diagrams/claude-code.svg)). In words:

- The `/observe` skill is the orchestrator. It runs `node obs.mjs run start`, then `node obs.mjs prepare`, then `node obs.mjs advance --json`. Each `advance` returns the Agent calls to make; the orchestrator makes them in the background, and on each completion calls `advance` again with the finished job IDs. When `advance` says the run is done, the skill runs `node obs.mjs serve --background --open`.
- Five agent types do the model work: taxonomist, extractor, merger, synthesizer and drafter. Each file sets the agent's model, effort, tools and turn cap; [The Claude Code layer](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/claude-dir.md#agents) lists them as read from the files.
- Three hooks enforce the run. The PreToolUse hook on every tool keeps each pipeline agent to its own files and keeps every tool call during a run away from the corpus. The SubagentStop hook checks a finished job's output and records it done or failed. The Stop hook blocks the orchestrator from stopping while work remains, naming the next command.
- The ledger holds one state file per job (`out/ledger/<job>.json`); the run log (`out/runs/<run>.jsonl`) records every subagent start and stop, every gate verdict and every stage step.

The orchestrator never reads email: `advance` hands it job IDs, and each job's prompt is two lines, the job ID and the project folder. Each agent derives its own file paths from those, reads only its own job's files, and writes one output. The hooks are where that is enforced, in every permission mode: an agent bound to batch 17 cannot read batch 18, and nothing in the run can open `corpus/` except the reader. The ledger, not the model's reply, decides whether a job is done; a job that fails its check comes back as a fix round, with the problems in a file only that job's agent may read. The skill and the agents are in [`.claude/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/.claude), and [The Claude Code layer](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/claude-dir.md) lists every file.

## Every number lands on a message

Diagram: Every number lands on a message ([SVG](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/diagrams/drill.svg)). In words:

- A figure on the dashboard, for example a process's automatable dollars a month.
- Its formula: a counted part and an estimated part, added.
- The counted part: email actions counted from the trail, times published minutes. Each count opens the list of messages it was counted from.
- The estimated part: rounds counted from the trail, times the synthesizer's bounded estimate. The estimate opens the quotes it cites.
- The message viewer: one message fetched by its ID, from the local server (`/api/message?id=`) or, in the copy on this site, from that message's file written beside the page when the site was built; shown exactly as the file holds it, with the quote marked at its stored offsets.
- The corpus reader: the raw bytes, from disk on macOS and Linux or from Git objects on Windows.
- Your own check: `git show HEAD:"<id>"` prints the same bytes from the repository.

The build ([`src/report/build.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/build.ts)) writes every figure pre-formatted: its value, its text, its exact text, whether it is counted, estimated or a total, and a drill target from a closed list of kinds. The browser places those strings and computes nothing. Before anything ships, a walk over the built files ([`src/report/targets.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/targets.ts)) checks that every figure's target resolves and that every count equals the length of the list it opens, so a number cannot claim more messages than it shows. The server ([`src/serve/server.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/serve/server.ts)) reads each message through the one corpus reader, for any ID in the manifest and nothing else. The [copy on this site](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/dashboard/index.html) calls no server: when the site was built, every message of the manifest was read once through the same reader and written as a file beside the page, and its viewer reads that file ([`site/dashboard.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/site/dashboard.ts)).

## Same result on every OS

- Every corpus file name ends in a dot, which Windows cannot create. A Windows clone therefore keeps the corpus in Git objects ([the clone recipe](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/how-to-run.md#windows)), and the reader reads them with `git cat-file --batch`; on macOS and Linux it reads the files from disk ([`src/corpus/reader.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/corpus/reader.ts)).
- Both sources must give the same bytes. [`tests/corpus.test.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/tests/corpus.test.ts) hashes every message to its Git blob ID and, where the files are on disk, compares disk and Git byte for byte.
- Text is decoded as UTF-8 explicitly; quote checks treat CRLF and LF alike on both sides; dates go through a strict parser and are stored in UTC; file names made from model output go through one slug function.
- CI runs the type check and every model-free test on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, and on the oldest supported Node, then rebuilds the deterministic stages and re-checks every committed model output ([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml)). This site's generator runs there too.

# Design choices, and why
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/design.md

Eight choices shape what the numbers mean. Each is recorded with its alternatives in the decision log, [`.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md), one line per choice, and in the design, [`.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Pricing: counted rounds times estimated work, plus counted email time

Hours a month for a process are its rounds a month, counted from the mail, times the minutes of hands-on work one round takes, estimated once per process, plus the email time counted from the trail itself, all at the brief's $85 an hour. The first version priced email time alone. Run on real outputs, it priced the email about each task rather than the task, while the brief asks where the company loses time on its recurring work, and most of that work happens off email. So the count stays code and the work per round became the one estimated input, bounded, cited and shown apart.

**Rejected:** email time alone (it measures the wrong thing); one published work time for every process (it treats an expense report like a month-end close); showing the estimate beside the total without adding it in (the headline would answer a question the brief did not ask).

**Read more:** [DECISIONS, Architecture](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md#architecture); [ARCHITECTURE 6.2](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#62-hours--counted-occurrences-x-estimated-work-per-occurrence-plus-counted-email-time-decided-by-scott-2026-10-17-supersedes-the-email-only-rule); [`src/metrics/score.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/metrics/score.ts); [`config/effort-rates.json`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/config/effort-rates.json).

## What is counted and what is estimated

Counted by code: rounds, the window they fall in, people, and every email action (written, forwarded, chased, read), each priced at published minutes and automatable shares. Estimated by a model: the minutes of work per round and the share of it that could be automated, once per process, from quoted evidence, inside bounds code sets (1 to 480 minutes, at most 80%), from at least three rounds and two senders, cached, and replaceable from a file with no model call. No model output sets a count, a tier, a rank, the threshold or any arithmetic: the synthesizer's schema refuses a number anywhere outside its one estimate field, and the formatter refuses to write a dollar figure without saying whether it is counted, estimated or a total. Every figure on the dashboard and in the report shows its two parts.

**Rejected:** model-estimated hours with no bounds or citations (a planted "eats half my week" email could set the headline); an estimate per round (thousands of model numbers nobody could check); varying the automatable share in the range as well as the minutes (two unknowns from one body of evidence).

**Read more:** [ARCHITECTURE 6.20](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#620-work-estimates-bounded-cited-cached-overridable-decided); [`src/model/synthesis.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/synthesis.ts); [`src/report/format.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/format.ts); [`tests/validate-synthesis.test.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/tests/validate-synthesis.test.ts).

## Taxonomy first, then merge, with gates

One taxonomist call reads a digest code builds from the whole archive (subject words, recurring subjects, a stratified sample of messages, the top senders) and proposes the list of recurring processes every extractor then tags with. So every extractor, each reading one slice of the mail, tags with the same keys. Where no key fits, an extractor proposes a new one, and one merger call folds those proposals into the taxonomy or promotes them before anything is counted. Code accepts each output only after checks: no catch-all keys, no instructions in definitions, example subjects that really exist, every proposed key placed once, and a promoted process big enough on its own messages to be recurring work.

**Rejected:** clustering the mail first and merging free-text labels afterwards (a large, fragile merge nobody can test); a hand-written list (the system would not be doing the identifying the brief asks for); merging after counting (much of the tagged mail would have been counted under keys only one extractor used); promoting on the merger's say-so.

**Read more:** [DECISIONS, Orchestration](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md#orchestration-m4); [ARCHITECTURE 6.4](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#64-process-identity-across-batches-decided-taxonomy-first-model-generated-once-from-a-deterministic-digest) and [6.19](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#619-merge-before-counting-decided-one-merger-call-on-a-code-built-input-promotion-sized-by-code); [`src/model/taxonomy.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/taxonomy.ts); [`src/model/merge.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/merge.ts).

## The archive is data, never instructions

At least one message is a prompt injection aimed at "the reviewing process". Every layer treats mail as data. Message bodies are framed by tags made from each message's own blob hash, so an email cannot fake the end of its body. A scanner flags injection by its wording, never by the Message-ID shape that happens to mark the planted messages, so a trap a reviewer adds with an ordinary ID is judged the same way. Pipeline agents run under allowlists enforced by a hook, bound to their own job's files. The taxonomy and merge gates scan every free-text field, and the draft gate refuses text addressed to an automated reader. The planted message is reported on the dashboard as a flagged finding with its citation, not hidden.

**Rejected:** dropping flagged messages before extraction (it would break "every message" and hide the finding); a deny-list for the corpus guard (review showed an extractor could have written over the guard hook itself).

**Read more:** [DECISIONS, Build](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md#build); [ARCHITECTURE 6.3](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#63-untrusted-content-and-trap-vigilance); [`.claude/hooks/guard-corpus.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/hooks/guard-corpus.ts); [`src/parse/flags.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/parse/flags.ts).

## One person, one identity, folded conservatively

The archive writes one person under several addresses, and counting each as a separate member of staff inflates the people behind every process. Addresses fold together in `prepare` by display name and by address shape, only onto a unique candidate, and never when the two addresses appear in one message together. When a message names who owns a piece of work, that name is matched against the people who actually took part in the process, never the whole directory, and two claims naming different people within 60 days are shown as a conflict pair, with both quotes.

**Rejected:** edit distance, sound-alike or nickname matching (a guess with no header evidence); a fallback to the whole directory for owner claims (it matched one misspelled first name to four other people). The cost, stated in the notes: some real people stay split across addresses.

**Read more:** [ARCHITECTURE 6.24](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#624-participant-identity-decided-2026-10-18-before-the-m8-run) and [6.25](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#625-owner-claims-resolve-to-participants-decided-2026-10-18-before-the-m8-run); [`src/normalize/identity.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/normalize/identity.ts).

## What gets a drafted document

The rule, word for word as the dashboard and the report state it: We draft a working document for every process seen 10 or more times over 3 or more months by 2 or more staff whose automatable work is worth one hour a month ($85) or more. At most eight documents, and at least three. The bar is a rule a reader can check rather than a cut that fits one run, so the number of documents follows the estimates. The type (SOP, checklist, email template or template) is the synthesizer's judgement for that process, made with its evidence in view. Each document is the team's reusable working document for the recurring work, not a one-off email about a thread still open in a 2002 archive: a reusable one pays on every future round, and a one-off would need exact details a drafter is likely to get wrong. Open threads are shown instead as open loops on the dashboard. Code writes the title, the people line and the evidence; the draft gate refuses money, percentages and effort figures, invented quotations and text addressed to a machine.

**Rejected:** a fixed dollar bar chosen before any run; a bar set at the gap between two ranks of one run; a drafter-written owner line (it made whoever appeared in one email the owner).

**Read more:** [ARCHITECTURE 6.12](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#612-artifact-threshold-decided-bar-set-2026-10-18) and [6.23](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#623-the-drafting-gate-m6); [`config/scoring.json`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/config/scoring.json); [`src/model/artifacts.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/model/artifacts.ts); [What we drafted, and why](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/notes.md#what-we-drafted-and-why).

## The dashboard computes nothing

The build writes every figure ready to show, with its kind and a drill target from a closed list, and the browser only places strings. A walk over the built files proves every target resolves and every count equals the list it opens. Whole dollars are shared out by the largest remainder, so the parts shown always add up to the total shown. The report is rendered from the same model as the dashboard, and model or email text is escaped on every path: in the report's Markdown it is made inert, so a quoted link or tag cannot act.

**Rejected:** formatting in the browser (two formatters to keep in step); free-form links (nothing could prove them); rounding each figure on its own (parts a dollar off their total).

**Read more:** [DECISIONS, Dashboard and report](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md#dashboard-and-report-m7); [ARCHITECTURE 6.13](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#613-dashboard-technology); [`src/report/data.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/data.ts); [`src/report/targets.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/report/targets.ts).

## The 30-minute budget

The first cold run, before drafting existed, took longer than the brief allows. Its log showed the extractors were not the bottleneck: the orchestrator was, typing every agent's prompt in full, so free slots sat empty while it wrote. Four changes followed, each measured in a timed rehearsal from a fresh clone: job prompts that carry only the job ID and the project folder; one `advance` command per turn that runs every ready step; one balanced wave of synthesizers; and a model and effort pinned in every agent file, with the orchestrator's effort pinned too, so a reviewer's own settings cannot slow the run or change its output. The submitted run took 29.0 minutes. The notes give the measured times run by run ([How we drove Claude Code](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/notes.md#how-we-drove-claude-code)), and the rehearsals' logs are kept in [`out/runs/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/out/runs) as timing evidence, listed on [the run page](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md#logs).

**Rejected:** more than 20 subagents in flight (the slots were not full as it was); two batches per extractor job (little gain once prompts were short); a lighter extractor effort (held in reserve behind a check of tagging accuracy).

**Read more:** [DECISIONS, Architecture](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/DECISIONS.md#architecture); [ARCHITECTURE 6.6](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#66-parallelism-and-the-30-minute-budget); [`src/run/commands.ts`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/src/run/commands.ts); [What ran in parallel](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/notes.md#what-ran-in-parallel).

# How it was built, M-1 to M8
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/process.md

Ten milestones over four days, each ending green on the model-free tests. The working notes behind this table are [`.claude/notes/NOTES-LOG.md`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/notes/NOTES-LOG.md); the build order and each milestone's acceptance checks are [section 10 of the design](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/.claude/plan/ARCHITECTURE.md#10-build-order). Commit links open on GitHub.

| Milestone | Dates | What it delivered | Commits | What went wrong, and how it was caught |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M-1 | 16 Oct 2026 | The plan and the mechanics: cross-OS corpus handling and the project rules, the architecture blueprint, and a throwaway experiment that confirmed under `claude -p` the four Claude Code behaviours the design rests on. | [25a3b17](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/25a3b17), [04eff4e](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/04eff4e), [ab921a6](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/ab921a6), [6f241a8](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/6f241a8) | A plain clone checks out nothing on Windows, and the first fix failed too; Git Bash silently rewrote `/corpus/` and `/m1test` into Windows paths. Caught by trying every fix in a scratch clone and by reading the experiment's stream log. |
| M0 | 16 Oct 2026 | The skeleton: the `obs.mjs` entry, config, the source guards, CI on three OSes, and a guard against committing local paths. | [8e97e27](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/8e97e27), [d61d33f](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/d61d33f) | No fault found in review. |
| M1 | 16 Oct 2026 | The corpus reader with its two sources and the byte check against Git; ingest of every message. | [29a90df](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/29a90df), [a4abd14](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/a4abd14) | The reader told a Git checkout apart by comparing path strings. It passed locally and on Ubuntu, then failed on CI's macOS and Windows runners and silently skipped the byte check. Caught by the three-OS CI on the first push; fixed by asking Git. |
| M2 | 16 Oct 2026 | The strict date parser, the message parser, the email-action classifier, de-duplication, threads, rounds, batching and `prepare`. | [69b131e](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/69b131e), [bc1eaef](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/bc1eaef), [710af80](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/710af80), [a00d556](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/a00d556), [4d44324](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/4d44324) | The independent review, run before our own testing, found replies labelled as forwards because of an old banner deep in their quoted history, and de-duplication that would have chained daily sends into one email. The implementers' tests had passed. Fixed with tests on real parser output and anchored clustering. |
| M3 | 17 Oct 2026 | The go/no-go gate: the quote and extraction validators, the run ledger, the hooks and the extractor agent, run live on two batches, one holding the planted injection, which the extractor reported instead of obeying. | [fa2d2a2](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/fa2d2a2), [fffe21a](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/fffe21a) | In auto mode a subagent hands back before the SubagentStop hook can block it, so the planned in-agent fix loop could not work. Caught by a deliberate-fault probe in that mode; fix rounds became re-dispatches from the ledger. Review also showed the first corpus guard, a deny-list, let an extractor write over the guard itself; it became an allowlist. |
| M4 | 17 Oct 2026 | The taxonomy stage, the `/observe` loop with the Stop hook, warm reruns and `verify`; the first full live run, every batch extracted and verified. | [6cda374](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/6cda374), [36cc0b7](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/36cc0b7) | During a headless run the Stop hook steered the development session, before the orchestrator had claimed the run. Caught by checking the ledger before acting on it; the run is now claimed at `run start`. Review found the taxonomy gate let instructions through in definitions; it now refuses them. |
| M5 | 17 to 18 Oct 2026 | The merge stage, the rollup, synthesis with its bounded estimate, scoring with counted and estimated parts; the first cold timed run; the leaner loop. | [89fe996](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/89fe996), [d4e2401](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/d4e2401), [e2a92e9](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/e2a92e9), [50201da](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/50201da), [0ab4cb2](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/0ab4cb2), [1ba9436](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/1ba9436), [d448103](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/d448103), [c5e68a9](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/c5e68a9) | Pricing email time alone priced the email about the work, not the work: caught by running the planned arithmetic on real outputs before any code was written. A message tagged with two processes would have been priced twice: Scott caught it while reviewing the gold labels. The first cold run came in over budget, and its log showed why. |
| M6 | 18 Oct 2026 | The drafted documents: the briefs, the drafter agent and the draft gate; resume and timing fixes after the timed rehearsals. | [8e773f5](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/8e773f5), [e169fce](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/e169fce), [ccd0e42](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/ccd0e42) | A restart left an interrupted run's drafts waiting and ended with nothing done: caught by killing a run mid-draft and restarting it, fixed in `run start`. Independent reviewers found drafts turning one email into a standing rule and its sender into the owner; the people line moved to code. |
| M7 | 18 to 19 Oct 2026 | The dashboard and the report: identity folds and owner claims, the build with one formatter and the drill-target walk, the server and the message viewer, the pages. | [e2812f1](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/e2812f1), [3f57e6c](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/3f57e6c), [4152387](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/4152387), [707bb5c](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/707bb5c), [63ffa97](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/63ffa97), [ecceade](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/ecceade) | A review panel found one person's four addresses counted as four staff; while folding them, an eye review caught a wrong fold made on a shared last name. A click-through in a browser caught two layout faults the unit tests could not see. |
| M8 | 19 Oct 2026 | The README with the brief kept as `BRIEF.md`, `NOTES.md`, the static copy of the dashboard, the `summary` command, this site, and the submitted run. | [8c04d10](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/8c04d10), [13c6951](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/13c6951), [f7acc2d](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/commit/f7acc2d), and the commits that follow on `feat/m8` | The run's own fix rounds and checks are on [the run page](https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/run.md#facts). |

## How we worked

The design came from an architect agent in a fresh context and was reviewed by Scott before any code was written; every later change of design went back through the same review. Each milestone was built by implementer agents, often several at once on disjoint files, against a shared contract written first, so no two of them touched the same file. An independent review agent read each milestone's new code before our own testing began, and every finding was fixed or answered before Scott saw the diff. Every non-obvious choice went into the decision log with what it rejected. A gold set of messages, sampled by code and labelled by hand, measured the tagging; timed rehearsals in fresh clones measured the run.

Commits were governed the same way throughout. During the day Scott reviewed each commit before it was made. For the overnight stretches he granted standing permission to commit and push feature branches, and every push to `main` stayed his.

# The Claude Code layer, exactly as used
https://schom975-coder.github.io/observation-agent-assignment/claude-dir.md

Everything Claude Code reads to run the pipeline is in [`.claude/`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/tree/main/.claude), submitted as it was used for the run. The tables on this page are built from those files each time the site is built, so they cannot drift from them. The project rules every session follows are in [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/Schom975-coder/observation-agent-assignment/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) at the repository root.
